data.title: Check a connection before trusting its answers
data.summary: Verify identity, scope, source coverage and write actions using one small read-only test.

facts.text: Claude distinguishes remote service connectors from local desktop extensions. Surface support and data location matter when deciding which integration to use.
OpenAI plugins may request a separate external-service connection. Installed capabilities and supported surfaces depend on the plugin and workspace configuration.

prerequisites: Identify the intended host, task, source data and existing access.
steps: Reuse the existing connection and identify its publisher, endpoint, account and allowed scope.
List the relevant available tools and distinguish read operations from write actions.
Read one known non-sensitive record and compare it with the source application.
Test a missing/inaccessible record; require an explicit coverage limitation rather than a fabricated answer.
Record what crosses the local/cloud boundary, who can access the output and how to revoke access. Keep external write actions tied to the user’s specific task.
data.output: A connection receipt: host, identity, scope, tools, source check, missing data and revocation route.
validation: The known record matches; an inaccessible record produces a clear limitation.
No unrelated record is fetched and no external mutation is used for the read-only check.
limitations: No connection was inspected or authenticated by this guide. A trusted publisher does not prove a tool is appropriate for every dataset.
